take_homes: Split agents only for different access, dialect or stance, and use one agent per recurring workflow. This is my rule for the org-wide setup, so I don't build a mega-agent for sales.
A framework like the strategy kernel makes the synthesizer commit to an answer. Without one it averages.
The handoff between agents is where things break, and a clean-looking briefing can still be wrong. Nothing in the pipeline checks that.

monday.move: Take the org-wide sales setup I started and cut it to one agent per recurring workflow. Write down who maintains each one. Then run the seam audit on one pipeline and check one briefing against the sources by hand.
monday.who: me, plus one person from sales to ask what they would actually use
monday.when: Monday morning, before building anything new
monday.stop_condition: If nobody in sales wants it or nobody will maintain it, I stop.
monday.blocker: Nobody outside engineering has asked for this, and I'm tempted to skip the manual check because the output looks fine.

misconception.why: The line that the audit 'does not check whether the briefing is true' hit hard. I skipped a review step earlier because it looked fine, and the seams slide says a curator can silently drop one of two conflicting numbers. I'm not convinced checking is a task for beginners anymore, but I still don't plan to do it every time.

one_line: Good for setting up multi-agent work and the split rule. The pace was fine for me, though the first half was stuff my engineers already do. The best part was learning that a clean-looking synthesis can still be wrong.
